title: Tracking Hypoxic Signaling within Encapsulated Cell Aggregates
protocol: Weigh 2g of PEG (linear, 10,000Da) into a 40mL glass vial with a hard plastic cap.
Add approximately 308μL of methacrylic anhydride and loosely cap the vial.
Microwave the vial on high for 2 minutes in a standard domestic microwave.
Thoroughly vortex the vial after microwaving.
Microwave the vial on high for an additional 5 minutes.
Allow the vial to cool enough to be handled with gloves.
Uncap the vial and slowly add methylene chloride while swirling the vial.
Add enough methylene chloride so that the solution appears clear and homogeneous, vortexing as needed.
Precipitate PEGDM in 200 mL of cold, stirred diethyl ether by adding the solution dropwise.
Collect the PEGDM by vacuum filtration and allow it to dry.
Dissolve the dried PEGDM in an adequate amount of deionized water (typically 100 -150 mL).
Dialyze the solution against deionized water for 5 days in dialysis tubing with a molecular weight cut-off of 1,000 Da.
Replace the water once daily during dialysis.
Aliquot the dialyzed solution into appropriate containers and freeze at -80°C overnight.
Lyophilize the frozen solution for 4 days to yield a purified white PEGDM powder.
Store the purified PEGDM powder at 4°C when not in use.
Prepare a 0.5 weight percent photoinitiator stock solution by dissolving Irgacure 2959 in deionized water.
Vortex the photoinitiator stock solution and store it in the dark.
Prepare a 10 wt% PEGDM and 0.025 wt% Irgacure 2959 solution in Hank's Balanced Salt Solution.
Vortex thoroughly to ensure dissolution of the PEGDM.
Filter the solution through a 0.2 μm syringe filter into a 1.8 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Wrap the tube in aluminum foil and store at 4°C.
Culture MIN6 cells in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 10% FBS, 7 mM glucose, 100 units/mL penicillin/streptomycin, and 0.5 μg/mL amphotericin B.
Incubate the culture at 37°C in a humidified environment with 5% CO2.
Aspirate the medium from the treated culture flask surface.
Rinse the cells with 37°C calcium/magnesium-free HBSS.
Add 2 mL of 37°C trypsin-EDTA solution to the cells and incubate for 3 minutes.
Firmly jar the side of the flask to knock the cells free.
Add 8 mL of 37°C medium to the cell suspension.
Pipette the cell suspension vigorously up and down, taking care not to introduce bubbles.
Transfer the cell suspension into a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube for cell counting.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer or other suitable method.
Determine the total number of cells to be infected.
Calculate the volume of virus suspension required to achieve the desired MOI (50 to 100 infectious particles per cell).
Dilute the virus in HBSS by carefully pipetting the proper amount of virus suspension into a pre-aliquoted volume of HBSS.
Disperse the cells by pipetting them up and down in their tube.
Pipette the necessary volume to achieve 400,000 cells per well into the wells of a 6-well suspension culture plate.
Add the appropriate volume of diluted virus to each well to achieve the desired MOI.
Add medium to each well to bring the total volume up to 1.7 mL.
Place the plate on an orbital shaker inside the incubator.
Set the shaker on a low setting so that the medium gently washes around the wells (˜100 rpm).
Allow the cells to aggregate for 24-36 hours.
Form aggregates with an approximate diameter of 75-175 μm.
Create a vessel by cutting the tapered tip off of a 1 mL plastic syringe and placing it open end up in a rack.
Pipette 20 μL of photoactive PEGDM solution into the open end of the syringe onto the plunger, ensuring the volume covers the entire plunger surface.
Adjust the plunger in small increments to achieve a flat fluid surface.
Place the syringe under a UV lamp (365nm, ˜7 mW/cm2) for approximately 8 minutes to allow hydrogel crosslinking.
Prepare cells by pipetting a volume containing the desired number of cells/aggregates into a 1.8 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Cap and centrifuge the tube at 130 g for 5 minutes.
Using a micropipettor, carefully remove the media without disturbing the cell pellet.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 20 μL of photoactive PEGDM solution.
Add the cell suspension to the syringe on top of the previously crosslinked hydrogel portion.
Expose the syringe to an additional 8 minutes of UV light to complete construction of the hydrogel.
When finished, the cells should be fully encapsulated within the cylindrical hydrogel.
Eject the hydrogel from the syringe and into 1 mL of HBSS in the well of a 24-well plate.
Briefly wash the gel with 1 mL of HBSS.
Transfer the gel to 1 mL of media in the well of a 24-well plate.
Culture the gel under the desired conditions.
Image the cells using fluorescent microscopy to track hypoxic signaling.
Image the cells in the multi-well plate or transfer the gel to a microscope slide before imaging.
Excite Ds Red at 556nm for optimal detection.
Observe peak emission at 586nm.
Monitor cells for initiation of protein production approximately 12 hours post induction.
Suspend dispersed MIN6 cells in 40 μL of photoactive PEGDM macromer solution.
Place the suspension in a decapitated 1 mL syringe.
Expose to 365 nm UV light for 10-12 minutes to form the hydrogel.
Remove the hydrogel disk from the syringe and wash it.
Incubate the hydrogel disk in a medium-filled well plate.
Form a half-gel by UV crosslinking of 20 μL of photoactive PEGDM macromer solution for 8 minutes.
Suspend MIN6 aggregates carefully in an additional 20 μL of photoactive macromer solution.
Add the suspended macromer and aggregates on top of the pre-formed half-gel.
Expose to 365 nm UV light for an additional 8 minutes to form the full gel.
